test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to NITI Aayog, what was the reduction in the Poverty Headcount Ratio in India from 2013-14 to 2022-23?
solution:
The correct answer is __**From 29.17% to 11.28%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to NITI Aayog, India's **Poverty Headcount Ratio** reduced significantly from **29.17% in 2013-14 to 11.28% in 2022-23**.
 
• This reduction is attributed to the government's focus on **poverty alleviation programs** and economic growth.
 
• The data reflects improved living standards across various demographics in India over the given period.
 
• The report emphasizes the importance of **targeted welfare schemes**, such as rural development initiatives, skill development programs, and employment generation schemes.
 
• This reduction aligns with India's commitment to achieving **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1**, which aims to eliminate poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty Headcount Ratio (PHCR):**

 
 
• PHCR measures the percentage of the population living below the **poverty line**.
 
• It is an important indicator used to assess poverty levels and monitor progress in poverty reduction.
 
 
 
• **Role of NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog is India's premier policy think tank that works on **socio-economic planning and sustainable development.**
 
• It provides data and analysis to inform policy decisions on poverty alleviation, health, education, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes Impacting Poverty:**
 
 
• Programs like **MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act)** and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** have contributed to poverty reduction.
 
• Skill development initiatives under **Skill India** have improved employment opportunities and incomes for low-income groups.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1:**
 
 
• SDG 1 aims to **end poverty in all its forms everywhere** by 2030.
 
• India's significant reduction in poverty aligns with global efforts to achieve SDG 1.
